Meeting header: 2026-12-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Ortiz (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood), Maya Singh (Catalyst Head of ML), David Kline (Platform), Rashida Noor (Product), Owen Park (Security)

Summary (auto): Align on POC acceptance criteria, benchmark plan, and deliverables.

[00:00] Samir: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Samir from Redwood Inference, i'll kick us off, jenna is our SE who will lead the eval and benchmarks
[00:18] Maya: thanks Samir, Maya here, quick note we have some regulatory constraints, so HIPAA and KMS hooks are real for us
[00:30] Jenna: yep noted. quick agenda: success criteria, golden prompts, regression strategy, load sizing, timeline. sound good?
[00:40] David: sounds good, also want to make sure we cover format enforcement, our downstream systems require strict JSON with FHIR-like fields
[00:53] Samir: great, first — success criteria. what would you consider a pass for this POC?
[01:05] Maya: three things: 1) accuracy / hallucination low — less than ~2% on our clinical extraction tasks, 2) p95 latency under 400ms for single-turn prompts, 3) zero format violations for schema outputs over a 99% rate
[01:28] Jenna: good, we usually separate scoring: relevance / correctness, hallucination, and format. we can do weighted scoring e.g. relevance 50, hallucination 30, format 20. does that map to your priorities?
[01:46] Maya: yes relevance heavier is fine, but hallucination has higher business cost, can we make hallucination threshold a hard gate rather than just weight?
[01:55] Jenna: yeah we can make hallucination a hard threshold: fail if above 2% on the regression set. the rest can be scored for pass/fail bands.
[02:08] Owen: and to be clear on PHI — we will only share pseudonymized/anonymized logs for the tests, and we need KMS integration for any keys if you host our private deployment
[02:22] Samir: absolutely. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we'll include the SOC2 and HIPAA addendum in the security pack.
[02:35] David: can you also include RBAC and SSO details? we use SAML via okta. sometimes transcripts show S S O slash Samuel in the auto transcript ha.
[02:46] Samir: (laughs) noted. we'll include SAML/Okta runbook.
[03:00] Jenna: moving on to golden prompts: we recommend 100-300 golden prompts that represent your core cases — extraction, summarization, and structured generation. ideally 60% extraction, 30% summarization, 10% edge transforms.
[03:21] Maya: ok we can do 200 to start, mixing clinical notes and triage forms. how do you want format constraints expressed? examples?
[03:34] Jenna: send us a CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output (or canonical JSON), tolerance notes. we'll provide a template. also include negative cases for hallucination tests.
[03:47] Liam: we'll give an example golden prompt and the eval harness. our eval harness can run scoring locally or on Redwood Console depending on where you want the data to live.
[04:01] David: for perf what does a typical benchmark look like? we see bursts up to 25 qps and steady 6 qps during office hours, avg token length ~120 tokens outbound per request
[04:19] Jenna: good data. for a realistic POC we run two benchmark types: 1) replay benchmark using your real traffic profile (sanitized) at target QPS, 2) golden-set correctness runs at low concurrency for accuracy metrics. replay we'll do a mini stress to your peak + 20% for safety. so plan for a ~30 minute stress run and 10k-50k tokens depending on your sample size.
[04:48] Rashida: timeline wise how long before we see results?
[04:54] Samir: proposed 4-week POC: week 0 (this week) prep/security + data handoff, week 1 golden set + smoke runs, week 2 replay/perf benchmarks, week 3 regression + final scoring and runbook handoff.
[05:13] Maya: that should work for our stakeholder timeline, execs want a preliminary pass within 3 weeks but full sign-off in 4.
[05:25] Jenna: scoring details — we'll run the golden set and compute per-prompt metrics: exact schema match rate, token-level hallucination flag, and human-annotated relevance on a 1-5 scale for a sample set. aggregate score will be weighted as discussed. we'll also run format parsers to count schema violations and surface examples.
[05:48] David: about quantization / model variants — what's the tradeoff? we care about cost but can't sacrifice hallucination/accuracy
[05:57] Jenna: we can test multiple model variants: base FP16 (higher cost, best perf), quantized int8 (cost savings) and a distilled variant if available. we recommend running correctness on FP16 and if acceptable, run perf and cost tests on quantized to measure delta. if hallucination goes up on quantized, we treat that as a hard fail for the variant.
[06:19] Maya: what about routing and fallbacks? we want predictable latency — can Redwood route to a lower-cost variant only when accuracy is intrinsically acceptable?
[06:30] Samir: yes, routing policies can be per-route; you can set latency SLOs and fallback to a compatible variant when capacity is constrained, or fall back to a cached answer. we'll demo routing rules and Canary splitting in the console.
[06:46] Owen: security question — where does data live during the replay benchmark? we need it to stay in our VPC or have a signed ingestion with customer-managed keys
[06:56] Jenna: for Redwood Private we can run the entire benchmark inside your VPC; for hosted we can accept sanitized logs via secure transfer and keys. we'll include the options in the security pack.
[07:10] Maya: ok good. one more thing — hallucination measurement. how do you detect a hallucination programmatically?
[07:20] Jenna: we use a hybrid approach: automated heuristics (fact-checking against the provided ground-truth where available), schema conformance (anything outside canonical fields flagged), and human review sampling. for clinical named entities we run a matcher against the ground-truth extraction; missing or invented entities increment the hallucination count.
[07:44] David: what's acceptable sample size for human review?
[07:49] Jenna: typically 200-500 samples for a statistically meaningful check on low-frequency failures; for high-sensitivity items we suggest 1k.
[07:58] Samir: action items recap — i'll send pricing/security, jenna will share golden-set template and eval script, catalyst to ship anonymized logs and the 200 golden prompts.
[08:09] Rashida: and we'll want a short decision checklist for execs that maps the weighted score to accept / manual review / reject.
[08:20] Jenna: we can produce that. we'll call it the POC acceptance matrix.
[08:26] Maya: perfect. any blockers we should raise now?
[08:30] Owen: just the KMS/keys policy — will need legal sign-off if we host keys.
[08:35] Samir: understood, include me and our legal contact on that thread.
[08:42] David: one small nit: can we run a tiny smoke test on dev next week before the larger replay? 15-20 minutes just to sanity check latency numbers
[08:52] Jenna: yes we'll set up a 15-min dev smoke test during week1, i'll coordinate with David after the call.
[09:00] Samir: ok last q, do you want Redwood Dedicated for this pilot or Hosted?
[09:07] Maya: prefer Hosted for speed unless security says otherwise; we might move to Dedicated for production if perf/cost justifies
[09:15] Samir: cool, we'll show both paths in the proposal.
[09:20] (crosstalk)
[09:25] Jenna: ok wrapping up — recap: deliver security pack + pricing (Samir), golden prompt template + eval harness (Jenna), Catalyst to give anonymized logs and golden prompts (Catalyst). schedule smoke test week of 12/14, replay perf week of 12/14-12/18, final runbook end of week 12/21.
[09:48] Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[09:52] Samir: thanks, we'll follow up in email and in the CRM.
